sections.h2: Who to call about your tax bill
sections.html:
Two county offices in Galena share the work. The Assessor builds the list of taxable property. The Collector of Revenue sends the bills and takes the payments.

  • Collector of Revenue: 108 E. 4th Street, P.O. Box 256, Galena, MO 65656; 417-357-6124. The courthouse is open weekdays from eight to four and closes for state and federal holidays.
  • Assessor: 106 E. 5th Street, P.O. Box 135, Galena, MO 65656; real estate line (417) 357-6145; personal property line (417) 357-6141; same weekday hours.

The yearly calendar runs like this. Assessment books normally close around July 1 and go to the County Clerk, who passes the figures to each taxing district. The districts then set their rates, typically by September 1. The Assessor has no say in those rates.

The Assessor also keeps the tax maps and adjusts property lines when the Recorder of Deeds forwards a warranty deed. The Collector's office has separate deputies for real estate, personal property, merchant licensing and the SB190 tax freeze. Ask for the real estate desk when you call about a house, and have the parcel number ready.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Payment is due by December 31. A bill still open on January 1 is delinquent. For 2026, statements were mailed on November 13 and online payment opened November 6.

Anything sent by post needs a U.S. Post Office postmark dated December 31 or earlier. A few practical points:

  • Card numbers are no longer taken verbally over the phone. Pay at the office or call the number printed on your statement.
  • Debit and credit card payments carry a fee of 2.4%, with a $1.95 floor.
  • A drop box at the north entrance of the Historic Courthouse is emptied daily.
  • A paid receipt can be printed, or shown on a phone, at the license bureau.

Read your statement for errors, including the mailing address. To change an address, call 417-357-6124.

sections.h2: Senior tax freeze and state credit
sections.html:
The application process for the Senior Citizen Property Tax Credit Freeze is closed right now. The Collector's staff includes a lead for the SB190 tax freeze, and that person is the one to ask about the next window.

Missouri also runs the Property Tax Credit Claim through the Department of Revenue. It refunds part of the tax or rent paid for some seniors, disabled owners and renters. Phone the Collector's office at 417-357-6124 to find out whether you fit either program before the next filing season.

sections.h2: How to appeal your assessed value
sections.html:
Phone the Assessor on (417) 357-6145 and ask for this year's Board of Equalization deadline. RSMo 138.060 tells the county board to decide valuation appeals in a summary way and says no presumption favors the assessor. Where a parcel's assessed value jumped by 15% or more over the previous assessment, other than through new construction or improvement, the assessor must show the figure is not above market value.

If you still owe the bill while you argue, RSMo 139.031 permits payment under protest. You pay the full bill before delinquency, send the collector a written statement of your reasons, and start a circuit court action within 90 days. An owner with a timely State Tax Commission appeal on file for that year skips the separate court action.

sections.h2: What happens if the bill goes past January 1?
sections.html: Penalties and interest start running. RSMo 140.150 allows delinquent land to go to sale each August, on the fourth Monday. The collector writes to the owner of record before publication, and the owner may clear the tax, penalty, interest and costs any time ahead of the sale.

If you sell while a bill is open, plan to pay it from closing proceeds. Ask the Collector for the exact payoff, since penalties change with the date, and give that number to the title company. The Collector takes payment at its Galena office and in the courthouse drop box.

Before you sign a contract, check three things. First, confirm the bill is paid or will be paid at closing. Second, if you are on the senior freeze, ask the Collector how a sale affects it. Third, make sure the Recorder has your earlier deeds on file, because the Assessor draws parcel lines from them. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so a clean tax record lets closing move at whatever pace you and the buyer choose.

sections.h2: A step by step plan for a seller
sections.html:
Start with the parcel number, which sits on your tax statement and is the quickest way to reach the right record at either office. Call the Collector at 417-357-6124 and ask whether the current year is paid, what is owed, and what the payoff would be on a given closing day. Then call the Assessor at (417) 357-6145 and ask whether any changes to the parcel, such as a new building or a lot split, are waiting to be recorded.

If the assessed value looks too high, ask for the Board of Equalization deadline before you list. A lower value saves money for whoever owns the house next, and a buyer's agent will often ask about the tax bill. Keep your statement, your payment receipt and any written appeal in one folder so you can hand them to the title company without a scramble.

At closing, the title company pays the Collector from your proceeds and the deed goes to the Recorder of Deeds in Galena. Recording the deed promptly keeps the Assessor's maps current, so the next bill goes to the right owner.

sections.h2: Growth and housing in Stone County
sections.html:
Population is rising: 31,079 in April 2020 and 32,503 in July 2025, a gain of 4.6%. Typical rent is $896, and owners report monthly costs of $1,451 with a mortgage and $476 without. The county counts 21,225 housing units but only 13,530 households, so many homes are not a household's usual address.

When you set a price, compare your parcel with sales of similar houses in your own community and school district rather than leaning on the county's $249,000 figure. Galena is the seat and Kimberling City the largest city. Branson West, Reeds Spring, Crane, Hurley and Blue Eye are the other towns, and school districts include Blue Eye R-V, Crane R-III, Galena R-II, Hurley R-I and Reeds Spring R-IV.

faqs.q: Where can I find the Stone County Collector?
faqs.a: At 108 E. 4th Street in Galena, or by mail at P.O. Box 256, Galena, MO 65656. Call 417-357-6124. Courthouse hours run weekdays, eight to four.

faqs.q: Do they take credit cards for property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, in person, online, or through the number on your statement. The fee is 2.4% with a $1.95 minimum, and no card numbers are given verbally by phone.

faqs.q: On what day does a Stone County bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: January 1. The bill is due by December 31, and mail needs a U.S. Post Office postmark of that date or earlier.

faqs.q: Which body decides the tax rate?
faqs.a: The taxing districts set it, usually by September 1. The county Assessor values property but has no part in rate setting.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the senior freeze today?
faqs.a: Not at the moment, because that application process is closed. Call 417-357-6124 to learn when it will reopen.
